title: Vanessa Van Edwards: The Conversation Habit That Makes Smart People Unlikable (Part 3)

lines.en: Wait, before we do level three, just want to close off on this uh do you talk too much test?
lines.zh: 等一下，在我們進到第三層之前，我想先把這個「你是不是話太多」測驗做個收尾。

lines.en: Okay, so I have a do you talk too much test in the book. It's right here.
lines.zh: 好，我書裡有一個「你是不是話太多」測驗。就在這裡。

lines.en: So, you're going to ask yourself, I leave a conversation realizing I don't know much about the other person. Okay,
lines.zh: 你要問自己：我離開一段對話時，發現我對對方了解不多。好，

lines.en: that's a secret curiosity question.
lines.zh: 那是一個隱藏的好奇心問題。

lines.en: So, there's five questions here.
lines.zh: 這裡有五個問題。

lines.en: And if you answer often more than three times, you're probably an overtalker. That's it.
lines.zh: 如果你有超過三題回答「經常」，你大概就是話太多的人。就這樣。

lines.en: And all of them secretly, Stephen, are saying, "Are you curious enough?" Okay? Right?
lines.zh: Stephen，而它們全都在暗中問：你夠好奇嗎？好嗎？對吧？

lines.en: Because we know that curiosity is the antidote.
lines.zh: 因為我們知道好奇心是解藥。

lines.en: So I put this right at the end of level one because you really can't go to level two if you're talking too much. Okay?
lines.zh: 所以我把它放在第一層的最後，因為如果你話太多，你就真的進不了第二層。好嗎？

lines.en: You're not curious enough. You're not going to learn their dream. So question one.
lines.zh: 你不夠好奇。你不會知道他們的夢想。所以第一題。

lines.en: So if I say yes to three of these, then I'm probably an overtalker. Correct?
lines.zh: 所以如果我有三題說是，我大概就是話太多的人。對嗎？

lines.en: So first one is I leave the conversation realizing I didn't know much about the other person. I'd say rarely.
lines.zh: 第一題是：我離開對話時，發現我對對方了解不多。我會說很少。

lines.en: After I finish speaking, people nod politely, but don't always respond. Sometimes.
lines.zh: 在我講完之後，大家會禮貌地點頭，但不一定會回應。有時候。

lines.en: I love telling long detailed stories, especially when people are too polite to interrupt.
lines.zh: 我很愛講又長又詳細的故事，尤其是當大家太客氣不好意思打斷的時候。

lines.en: Do you ever tell a long detailed story?
lines.zh: 你有講過又長又詳細的故事嗎？

lines.en: Only when I'm on stage and I'm and someone has paid me to. That doesn't count. Okay. Doesn't count.
lines.zh: 只有在台上、有人付錢給我的時候。那不算。好。不算。

lines.en: Sometimes I'd say, um, I've been told gently or not so gently that I talk a lot. Rarely.
lines.zh: 我會說有時候。嗯，有人委婉或不太委婉地跟我說過我話很多。很少。

lines.en: I've never been told that.
lines.zh: 從來沒人跟我說過。

lines.en: Number five, while I'm midstory, I notice people glance around the room sometimes. So, you pass. Okay.
lines.zh: 第五題：在我講故事講到一半時，我注意到大家會環顧四周。有時候。所以你過關了。好。

lines.en: Now, I could have told you that also, but yeah, you pass.
lines.zh: 其實我也可以直接跟你說，但對，你過關了。

lines.en: So, those it's really important because it might be creating conversational friction, right? Especially at work.
lines.zh: 所以這些真的很重要，因為它可能在製造對話摩擦，對吧？尤其是在職場上。

lines.en: And the best muscle you can do is asking more, talking less.
lines.zh: 你能鍛鍊的最好的肌肉，就是多問、少說。

lines.en: And a challenge, a very specific challenge,
lines.zh: 還有一個挑戰，一個非常具體的挑戰，

lines.en: please do a yap challenge.
lines.zh: 請做「碎念挑戰」。

lines.en: Do you know what a yap challenge is? Oh, a yap challenge.
lines.zh: 你知道碎念挑戰是什麼嗎？喔，碎念挑戰。

lines.en: A yeah challenge is you open up your phone camera and you teach something or share an opinion about something without notes and you hit record.
lines.zh: 碎念挑戰就是打開手機相機，不看筆記，教一件事或分享你對某件事的意見，然後按下錄影。

lines.en: If you go naturally 15 or 30 seconds, you're probably good.
lines.zh: 如果你自然地講 15 或 30 秒，你大概沒問題。

lines.en: If you're hitting 45 seconds, that's the max.
lines.zh: 如果你講到 45 秒，那是上限。

lines.en: If you're up to a minute or 2 minutes, you probably talk too much.
lines.zh: 如果你講到一分鐘或兩分鐘，你大概話太多了。

lines.en: H about yourself or just
lines.zh: 嗯，是講自己，還是就……

lines.en: about yourself about like that.
lines.zh: 講自己之類的。

lines.en: That your typical answering length is longer than conversationally appropriate
lines.zh: 就是你通常回答的長度比對話中適當的長度還長，

lines.en: to a question about you.
lines.zh: 針對關於你的問題。

lines.en: It a yap challenge could be share your opinion about veganism.
lines.zh: 碎念挑戰可以是：分享你對純素主義的看法。

lines.en: Damn, I didn't think I could get that done in 15 seconds. What's your answer? No, not to veganism.
lines.zh: 天啊，我不覺得我能在 15 秒內講完。你的答案是什麼？不，不是純素主義。

lines.en: Just generally like if it's an idea, everything in my head is a story first. So, it's like, you know what though? Introverts can. Introverts absolutely can.
lines.zh: 就是一般來說，如果是一個想法，我腦中所有東西都會先變成一個故事。所以就像……你知道嗎？內向的人做得到。內向的人絕對做得到。

lines.en: And they'll often go too short. Okay.
lines.zh: 而且他們常常講得太短。好。

lines.en: Like for example, I'll give I'll give you a yap challenge that I was just thinking about the other day and we're going to do it on social media.
lines.zh: 例如，我給你一個碎念挑戰，是我前幾天才在想的，我們會把它放到社群媒體上。

lines.en: We'll do it together. Yap challenge.
lines.zh: 我們一起做。碎念挑戰。

lines.en: Someone recently asked my friend out by asking for her Instagram handle, not her number. Agree or disagree? It depends on her vibe.
lines.zh: 最近有人約我朋友出去，是跟她要 Instagram 帳號，而不是電話號碼。同意還是不同意？要看她的氣場。

lines.en: Was she what how what energy was she giving and what was the context?
lines.zh: 她是怎麼樣的、散發什麼能量、當時的情境是什麼？

lines.en: Was that after a 2-hour date? Was that
lines.zh: 是在兩小時的約會之後嗎？還是

lines.en: just meeting her on the street?
lines.zh: 只是在路上剛認識她？

lines.en: Rolled up on the street.
lines.zh: 在路上直接走過去。

lines.en: I think it's actually I agree then because it's less invasive.
lines.zh: 我覺得那我其實同意，因為這比較不具侵犯性。

lines.en: It's like I will earn your number. Oh. Oh wow.
lines.zh: 就像是：我會努力贏得你的電話號碼。喔。喔，哇。

lines.en: Give me the chance to earn your number. Okay. You just convinced me. That's interesting.
lines.zh: 給我一個贏得你電話號碼的機會。好。你剛剛說服我了。很有意思。

lines.en: So, by the way, I think that was what 12 seconds. Okay. Yeah, maybe. Right.
lines.zh: 順帶一提，我想那大概是 12 秒。好。對，也許吧。對。

lines.en: So, like you you're keeping it tight. I disagree.
lines.zh: 所以你講得很精簡。我不同意。

lines.en: But that that is an interesting nuance.
lines.zh: 但那是一個有意思的細微差別。

lines.en: I'm not going to give you my Instagram because my Instagram is performative. Everyone's Instagram is performative.
lines.zh: 我不會給你我的 Instagram，因為我的 Instagram 是一種表演。每個人的 Instagram 都是一種表演。

lines.en: If you are looking at my Instagram, it's like saying, "I don't want to get to know you through conversation.
lines.zh: 如果你在看我的 Instagram，就好像在說：「我不想透過對話認識你。

lines.en: I'm going to look through everything and know everything about you before I decide if I want to take you out."
lines.zh: 我要在決定要不要約你出去之前，先把所有東西看一遍、知道你的一切。」

lines.en: And you take the joy out of discovery.
lines.zh: 這樣你就把發現的樂趣拿掉了。

lines.en: If I'm with you and I'm like, "Do you have any pets?"
lines.zh: 如果我和你在一起，我說：「你有養寵物嗎？」

lines.en: And you're like, "Yeah, I have a dog."
lines.zh: 你說：「有，我有一隻狗。」

lines.en: Then I can, "Oh, how'd you get the dog? What's the dog's name?
lines.zh: 然後我就可以問：「喔，你怎麼會養這隻狗？牠叫什麼名字？

lines.en: How'd you choose that name?"
lines.zh: 你怎麼取這個名字的？」

lines.en: Versus, "Uh, look, she has a dog named Stewie."
lines.zh: 而不是：「呃，你看，她有一隻叫 Stewie 的狗。」

lines.en: But you know, your number is reserved for people in your like personal professional life.
lines.zh: 但你知道，你的電話號碼是留給你個人和工作生活中的人。

lines.en: So, what you're saying if you roll up on the street is you're saying, "Let me in to your personal and professional environment, stranger."
lines.zh: 所以如果你在路上直接走過去要電話，你是在說：「陌生人，讓我進入你的個人和工作環境吧。」

lines.en: Whereas the public environment, which is Instagram,
lines.zh: 而公開的環境，也就是 Instagram，

lines.en: is I think a much more socially appropriate place to invite oneself into.
lines.zh: 我覺得是一個在社交上更適合主動加入的地方。

lines.en: Okay, let's fight about this. Okay,
lines.zh: 好，我們來辯論這個。好，

lines.en: if you do that, your conversation is going to be more awkward on your first date because
lines.zh: 如果你這樣做，你們第一次約會的對話會更尷尬，因為

lines.en: because you feel like you've already learned about the person.
lines.zh: 因為你覺得你已經了解這個人了。

lines.en: So maybe you're discovering more of their public persona, but you've seen their kind of friends, where they hang out, what they do on the weekends, do they hike or not, do they have any pets?
lines.zh: 也許你看到的比較多是他們的公開形象，但你已經看過他們的朋友、他們常去哪裡、週末做什麼、有沒有去健行、有沒有養寵物。

lines.en: Oh, look, there they are at Thanksgiving.
lines.zh: 喔，你看，這是他們過感恩節。

lines.en: They have lots of siblings.
lines.zh: 他們有很多兄弟姊妹。

lines.en: This is, I think, why we're having awkward first date conversations, why first dates have gotten even worse, is because you're on the first date, you've already discovered all level one stuff that you think you know.
lines.zh: 我覺得這就是為什麼我們第一次約會的對話很尷尬、為什麼第一次約會變得更糟，因為你在第一次約會時，已經發掘了所有你以為你知道的第一層資訊。

lines.en: So now, even though you have your very first conversation, you you kind of have to go to level two, it's so much harder and it's unnatural.
lines.zh: 所以現在，雖然這是你們的第一次對話，你卻有點得直接進到第二層，這難多了，而且很不自然。

lines.en: It's unnatural to know all this information that wasn't transmitted human to human that was done in a performative way.
lines.zh: 知道這些不是人與人之間傳遞、而是用表演方式得到的資訊，是很不自然的。

lines.en: And then you have to get in person and it's harder to come up with conversation starters because you already know a lot.
lines.zh: 然後你們得面對面，而要想出開場白更難，因為你已經知道很多了。

lines.en: I also think what I would say is if someone were I'm not single.
lines.zh: 我也覺得我會說，如果有人……我不是單身。

lines.en: I haven't been single a long time.
lines.zh: 我已經很久不是單身了。

lines.en: But if someone were to say, "Can I have your Instagram?"
lines.zh: 但如果有人說：「可以給我你的 Instagram 嗎？」

lines.en: I would say, you know, I I have one for just friends and family, but maybe you can get there one day. You would say that?
lines.zh: 我會說：你知道，我有一個只給朋友和家人的帳號，但也許有一天你可以進來。你會這樣說？

lines.en: Yeah, I would. No, I never
lines.zh: 對，我會。不，我從不……

lines.en: because I want you to chat me, right?
lines.zh: 因為我想要你跟我聊天，對吧？

lines.en: Like I don't want to show you my Instagram. we're going to see everything and like I'd rather like like let's banter like let's chat are you funny?
lines.zh: 我不想給你看我的 Instagram，那樣我們就會看到所有東西，我寧願我們來打趣、來聊天，你好笑嗎？

lines.en: Are you going to ask me good questions?
lines.zh: 你會問我好問題嗎？

lines.en: Are you going to be a conversational narcissist?
lines.zh: 你會是個對話型自戀者嗎？

lines.en: And then ask me at dinner if it's going well over text or over over the phone.
lines.zh: 然後如果傳訊息或講電話聊得不錯，再約我吃晚餐。

lines.en: So you think less context results in better conversation?
lines.zh: 所以你覺得背景資訊越少，對話越好？

lines.en: So just having their WhatsApp or their iMessage is going to result in more interesting conversations than me knowing that you like hiking and puppies and me being able to be like, "Have you got a Labradoodle, too?"
lines.zh: 所以只有他們的 WhatsApp 或 iMessage，會比我知道你喜歡健行和小狗、然後可以說「你也有一隻拉布拉多貴賓嗎？」帶來更有趣的對話？

lines.en: Oh my god, my Labradoodle is just given birth to a couple of triplets. Yes. And less performative context.
lines.zh: 天啊，我的拉布拉多貴賓剛生了三胞胎。對。而且表演性質的背景資訊比較少。

lines.en: Like our social feeds are not 100% real.
lines.zh: 我們的社群動態不是百分之百真實的。

lines.en: So it's not like you were listening to me talk about something.
lines.zh: 所以那不像是你在聽我聊某件事。

lines.en: It's a perform it's a curated highlight reel of my life.
lines.zh: 那是一段表演，是我人生精心挑選的精華片段。

lines.en: So you feel like you know me.
lines.zh: 所以你會覺得你認識我。

lines.en: Like people who follow me on Instagram like they might feel like they know me, but my life is quite different than my Instagram in the sense of I show a very small piece of what I do.
lines.zh: 像在 Instagram 上追蹤我的人，可能會覺得他們認識我，但我的生活和我的 Instagram 很不一樣，因為我只展示了我做的事裡很小的一部分。

lines.en: Same right with you, right?
lines.zh: 你也一樣，對吧？

lines.en: And so I know I'm not single, but if I was single and someone asked for my my Instagram, even as a not like public figure,
lines.zh: 所以我知道我不是單身，但如果我是單身，有人跟我要 Instagram，就算我不是什麼公眾人物，

lines.en: I would have no casual level one banter with them that is critical, socially critical for me to understand their basics.
lines.zh: 我和他們就沒有任何輕鬆的第一層打趣，而那對我了解他們的基本資訊在社交上至關重要。

lines.en: And so when we skip level one, we do damage to our potential connection later.
lines.zh: 所以當我們跳過第一層，我們就在傷害之後可能的連結。

lines.en: We create more awkwardness and more friction for ourselves. Okay?
lines.zh: 我們為自己製造了更多尷尬和摩擦。好嗎？

lines.en: So my challenge for single people is stop asking for handles and ask for numbers.
lines.zh: 所以我給單身者的挑戰是：別再要帳號了，要電話號碼。

lines.en: Are people going to get mad at me?
lines.zh: 大家會生我的氣嗎？

lines.en: Well, a lot of them are meeting via dating apps now. For sure.
lines.zh: 嗯，現在很多人是透過交友軟體認識的。當然。

lines.en: And that I think that's okay, right?
lines.zh: 我覺得那沒關係，對吧？

lines.en: You know, a dating app is much more limited than an endless feed.
lines.zh: 你知道，交友軟體比無止盡的動態消息有限得多。

lines.en: It's like I don't know how many photos are on dating apps these days, but still like that's like the most performative.
lines.zh: 我不知道現在交友軟體上有多少張照片，但那仍然是最具表演性的。

lines.en: It's like look at me at the gym.
lines.zh: 就像：看我在健身房。

lines.en: Look at this car that I bought. Look at But it's not forever.
lines.zh: 看我買的這台車。看……但那不是無止盡的。

lines.en: Like you can't go back to someone's Instagram since they were in high school, right?
lines.zh: 你沒辦法回頭翻某人從高中開始的 Instagram，對吧？

lines.en: Like it's, you know, it's six images or 10 images.
lines.zh: 就是，你知道，只有六張或十張照片。

lines.en: You have these pre-subscribed questions.
lines.zh: 有一些預設好的問題。

lines.en: Like I'm actually okay with I love dating apps.
lines.zh: 我其實可以接受，我很喜歡交友軟體。

lines.en: I think that actually they can really connect people very quickly.
lines.zh: 我覺得它們其實能很快地讓人建立連結。

lines.en: But you don't know everything about you.
lines.zh: 但你不會知道對方的一切。

lines.en: You don't feel like you know everything about me.
lines.zh: 你不會覺得你知道我的一切。

lines.en: I feel like people on dating apps hate dating apps. Of course. Of course.
lines.zh: 我覺得用交友軟體的人都很討厭交友軟體。當然。當然。

lines.en: But how else are we going to meet people if we have our AirPods in all the time?
lines.zh: 但如果我們一直戴著 AirPods，還能怎麼認識人？

lines.en: You're not going to meet people if you're at the gym.
lines.zh: 你在健身房不會認識人的。

lines.en: We talked about this last time.
lines.zh: 我們上次聊過這個。

lines.en: If you have your AirPods in at the gym and someone wants to hit on you, you're not going to hear it.
lines.zh: 如果你在健身房戴著 AirPods，有人想搭訕你，你根本聽不到。

lines.en: So, we have to use dating apps.
lines.zh: 所以我們得用交友軟體。

lines.en: I think they're the only way that we'll be able to connect.
lines.zh: 我覺得那是我們唯一能建立連結的方式。

lines.en: So, I I'm actually I'm pro dating app.
lines.zh: 所以我其實支持交友軟體。

lines.en: Of course, I would love for people to approach in person, but I'm not pro not talking first.
lines.zh: 當然，我很希望大家能當面搭訕，但我不支持不先聊天。

lines.en: And I think if someone asks for your handle, you're fair to say it's just for my friends and family.
lines.zh: 而且我覺得如果有人跟你要帳號，你可以說那只給朋友和家人。

lines.en: Let's try to get there. Okay, I concede.
lines.zh: 我們試著走到那一步吧。好，我認輸。

lines.en: No, I think you it makes sense. It doesn't make sense. It's hard to repeat.
lines.zh: 不，我覺得你說得有道理。沒道理。很難重複一遍。

lines.en: Okay, so this is a wonderful level, but it's reserved for your most important people.
lines.zh: 好，所以這是很美好的一層，但它是留給你最重要的人的。

lines.en: I think a mistake that people make is they are afraid of going too deep too quickly and they're afraid of going deep deep in conversation because it feels scary to be vulnerable.
lines.zh: 我覺得大家常犯的一個錯，是害怕太快太深入，害怕在對話中聊得很深，因為示弱的感覺很可怕。

lines.en: And are they right? They are right. Okay.
lines.zh: 他們的擔心對嗎？對。好。

lines.en: If we go too deep too quickly, especially at work, and I wrote this book with work in mind, people are going to think you're weird.
lines.zh: 如果我們太快太深入，尤其是在職場上，而我寫這本書時想著的就是職場，大家會覺得你很怪。

lines.en: If we share too much too quickly, it's going to be weird.
lines.zh: 如果我們太快分享太多，就會很怪。

lines.en: And there is such a thing as vulnerability regret.
lines.zh: 確實有「示弱後悔」這種東西。

lines.en: Vulnerability regret is you shared something too vulnerable and it wasn't a safe space or it wasn't received well.
lines.zh: 示弱後悔就是你分享了太脆弱的事，但那不是安全的空間，或對方沒有好好接住。

lines.en: And the heartache that you get from that is soul crushing. Right?
lines.zh: 那種心痛會讓人心力交瘁，對吧？

lines.en: If you share something too or you ask something to deep too quickly, you're like, why did I do it's painful. Has that ever happened?
lines.zh: 如果你太快分享了太多，或太快問了太深的問題，你會想：我為什麼要……好痛苦。有發生過嗎？

lines.en: Does that happen to you or No, you don't share. Uh, no.

lines.zh: 我曾經在離開一些場合後想，其實那也許不是分享那件事的適當場合。

lines.zh: 我馬上想到兩週前的一場會議，我在面試一個人，面試的前 25 分鐘，他們分享了一些關於很小的童年時期、非常非常私人的事，我嗯……

lines.en: I almost had to adjust myself
lines.zh: 我幾乎得調整自己，

lines.en: to like meet them and ask them about work stuff but I I almost felt myself pivoting away being like oh my gosh I have to be

lines.en: more of a a counselor or something. Yeah.

lines.zh: 所以我覺得我們其實得替第三層設個門檻，對吧？

lines.en: I think we actually have to gate and and it's been a little confusing culturally because I think that we are loving vulnerability and that that's really good and vulnerability and authenticity.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們真的得設門檻，這在文化上有點讓人困惑，因為我覺得我們很推崇示弱，這很好，示弱和真誠。

lines.en: There's a very fine line there.
lines.zh: 這兩者之間只有一線之隔。

lines.en: Like being authentic is great, but being too vulnerable too quickly is very awkward and sometimes not safe.
lines.zh: 真誠很好，但太快太脆弱會非常尷尬，有時也不安全。

lines.en: So I really share when we talk about level three, I want you to reserve it for your most important people. Okay?
lines.zh: 所以當我們談第三層時，我真的希望你把它留給你最重要的人。好嗎？

lines.en: So level three is called your self-narrative.
lines.zh: 第三層叫做「自我敘事」。

lines.en: Your self-narrative is the story you tell yourself about yourself.
lines.zh: 你的自我敘事是你告訴自己關於自己的故事。

lines.en: It is how you make sense of your journey and purpose in life.
lines.zh: 它是你如何理解自己人生的旅程和目的。

lines.en: And the story you tell yourself about yourself is self-creating.
lines.zh: 而你告訴自己關於自己的故事，會自我實現。

lines.en: Meaning, if you have a narrative of hardship and being unlucky, you are probably going to see more hardship and create more bad luck for yourself.
lines.zh: 意思是，如果你的敘事是艱難和倒楣，你大概就會看到更多艱難，也為自己製造更多厄運。

lines.en: And they've proven that this there's actually two types of selfnarratives.
lines.zh: 研究已經證明，其實有兩種自我敘事。

lines.en: There's a contamination narrative and a redemption narrative.
lines.zh: 一種是「污染敘事」，一種是「救贖敘事」。

lines.en: People with a redemption narrative, they have a frame around the facts of their life of no matter what they do,
lines.zh: 擁有救贖敘事的人，會用一個框架看待自己人生中的事實：不管他們做什麼，

lines.en: no matter what comes their way, they're going to overcome with hard work and grit and resilience, they can overcome anything.
lines.zh: 不管遇到什麼，他們都能靠努力、毅力和韌性克服，他們能克服任何事。

lines.en: And what's interesting about this in our research is this narrative, it holds across their life.
lines.zh: 而在我們的研究中，有意思的是這種敘事會貫穿他們的一生。

lines.en: Yes, they're they're facts of their life, but their work, their love, their parenting, they repeat that same redemption narrative in everything they do.
lines.zh: 對，那些是他們人生的事實，但在工作、愛情、育兒上，他們在做的每件事中都重複著同樣的救贖敘事。

lines.en: The other kind of narrative is a contamination narrative.
lines.zh: 另一種敘事是污染敘事。

lines.en: People with a contamination narrative, they feel that all the hardship and all the challenge and the struggle has happened to them and they can't make it through.
lines.zh: 擁有污染敘事的人，會覺得所有的艱難、挑戰和掙扎都發生在他們身上，而他們撐不過去。

lines.en: They can't overcome.
lines.zh: 他們無法克服。

lines.en: That no matter how hard they've worked, their grit, their strength, their resilience, they're a victim of circumstance. they typically feel very unlucky and very out of control.
lines.zh: 不管他們多努力、多有毅力、多堅強、多有韌性，他們都是環境的受害者。他們通常覺得自己非常倒楣、非常無法掌控。

lines.en: And when you have that kind of narrative, it's less about the facts of your life and more about the frames of your life, how you're seeing those facts.
lines.zh: 當你有那種敘事時，重點比較不在你人生中的事實，而在你人生的框架，也就是你怎麼看待那些事實。

lines.en: When you have a contamination narrative or you're in a relationship with someone with a with a contamination narrative, the only way that I think we can change that, cuz our narratives are changeable.
lines.zh: 當你有污染敘事，或是你和一個有污染敘事的人在一起，我覺得唯一能改變它的方法，因為我們的敘事是可以改變的，

lines.en: These are not fixed personality traits, is via conversation.
lines.zh: 這些不是固定的人格特質，就是透過對話。

lines.en: So, my secret hope with with level three conversation is when you're in a safe relationship, when you can truly share who you are, when you feel understood, you can maybe rewrite your narrative.
lines.zh: 所以我對第三層對話暗自的期望是，當你處在一段安全的關係中，當你能真正分享你是誰，當你覺得被理解，你也許就能改寫你的敘事。

lines.en: You can maybe flip from a contamination narrative, the frame of how you've seen your facts into redemption.
lines.zh: 你也許能從污染敘事，也就是你看待事實的框架，翻轉成救贖敘事。

lines.en: And that is my secret goal here.
lines.zh: 這就是我在這裡暗自的目標。

lines.en: So, how do we do that?
lines.zh: 那我們要怎麼做？

lines.en: Okay, the first thing is beginning to uncover what your narrative is and what someone else's narrative is.
lines.zh: 好，第一件事是開始發掘你的敘事是什麼、別人的敘事是什麼。

lines.en: So the first thing we have to understand is how our brain works. Our brains are storytellers.
lines.zh: 我們首先得了解大腦如何運作。我們的大腦是說故事的人。

lines.en: Our that's why we love story.
lines.zh: 這就是為什麼我們愛故事。

lines.en: And level one, it was kind of a warm-up.
lines.zh: 而第一層有點像暖身。

lines.en: Like when we're telling story about our passions and our side hustles, we're also telling a story about ourselves all the time. Mhm.
lines.zh: 當我們在講關於自己熱情和副業的故事時，我們其實也一直在講關於自己的故事。嗯。

lines.en: And so we've told a story about ourselves.
lines.zh: 所以我們講了一個關於自己的故事。

lines.en: And there are what I call narrative hints.
lines.zh: 而有一些我稱之為「敘事線索」的東西。

lines.en: In conversation, people will leak the kind of narrative that they have.
lines.zh: 在對話中，人們會不經意洩漏自己擁有的那種敘事。

lines.en: So they might say, "Oh, everyone always zigs and I zag.
lines.zh: 他們可能會說：「喔，大家都往東，我偏往西。

lines.en: Gosh, everything bad always happens to me."
lines.zh: 天啊，壞事總是發生在我身上。」

lines.en: Oh, of course, of course. Yet another thing.
lines.zh: 「喔，當然，當然。又來了。」

lines.en: If people have superlatives, always, never, they tend to be more of a contamination person.
lines.zh: 如果人們用最高級的詞，像「總是」「從不」，他們往往比較偏向污染敘事的人。

lines.en: People who are in that contamination narrative space, they tend to see things as very black and white.
lines.zh: 處在污染敘事的人，往往把事情看得非常非黑即白。

lines.en: They tend to see things as permanent versus redemption people tend to leak positive hints and they feel very lucky.
lines.zh: 他們往往把事情看成永久的，而救贖型的人則會洩漏正向的線索，他們覺得自己很幸運。

lines.en: They say, "Oh, good things always happen to me."
lines.zh: 他們會說：「喔，好事總是發生在我身上。」

lines.en: Or, "There's always a silver lining. Oh, yeah.
lines.zh: 或是：「凡事總有一線希望。喔，對。

lines.en: You know, just my luck. I got it." Right?
lines.zh: 你知道，我就是這麼好運，我拿到了。」對吧？

lines.en: They're saying things about how it's happening. They're leaking their narratives.
lines.zh: 他們在說事情是怎麼發生的。他們在洩漏自己的敘事。

lines.en: Who ends up being more successful, happy, and healthy? Absolutely.
lines.zh: 誰最後會更成功、更快樂、更健康？絕對是

lines.en: People with redemptive redemptive narratives.
lines.zh: 擁有救贖敘事的人。

lines.en: They have found that people with redemption narratives, they live longer.
lines.zh: 研究發現，擁有救贖敘事的人活得更久。

lines.en: They have better immune systems. They have better connections. They feel happier.
lines.zh: 他們的免疫系統更好，人際連結更好，也覺得更快樂。

lines.en: And that is because they feel they can handle whatever is thrown at them.
lines.zh: 那是因為他們覺得不管遇到什麼，他們都能應付。

lines.en: They have a great internal locus of control.
lines.zh: 他們有很強的內在控制感。

lines.en: They feel that no matter what comes at them, they can handle it.
lines.zh: 他們覺得不管遇到什麼，都能處理。

lines.en: And the good news is this is learnable, right?
lines.zh: 好消息是，這是可以學的，對吧？

lines.en: If we begin to talk about our narratives with our children, with our partners, we can begin to teach them actually you have growth here.
lines.zh: 如果我們開始和孩子、伴侶談論我們的敘事，我們就能開始教他們：其實你在這方面可以成長。

lines.en: You have agency over your narrative.
lines.zh: 你對自己的敘事有主導權。

lines.en: This internal locus of control thing is something that I learned about when I was probably 16 or 17 in psychology class. Yeah.
lines.zh: 這個內在控制感，是我大概 16、17 歲在心理學課上學到的。對。

lines.en: And what does it mean?
lines.zh: 它是什麼意思？

lines.en: And what what does the study say about the importance of it?
lines.zh: 研究怎麼說它的重要性？

lines.en: So an internal locus of control means that you feel that you're in control.
lines.zh: 內在控制感的意思是你覺得自己能掌控。

lines.en: You have agency over your decisions, over what happens to you, that things can happen to you in your life, but you can decide how you interact with them.
lines.zh: 你對自己的決定、對發生在你身上的事有主導權，人生中會有事情發生在你身上，但你可以決定如何應對。

lines.en: You can decide how you behave.
lines.zh: 你可以決定自己的行為。

lines.en: People with an external locus of control get their worth from outside sources.
lines.zh: 外在控制感的人，是從外在來源獲得自我價值。

lines.en: They feel validated when someone else tells them they look good.
lines.zh: 別人說他們看起來很好時，他們才覺得被肯定。

lines.en: They feel good when someone else tells them they're doing good.
lines.zh: 別人說他們做得很好時，他們才覺得好。

lines.en: They're looking for external ways to feel better.
lines.zh: 他們在找外在的方式讓自己感覺更好。

lines.en: They look more at like for example vanity metrics, their likes or their follows, how many friends they have, how often they're invited, are they getting compliments?
lines.zh: 他們比較看重像是虛榮指標，按讚數、追蹤數、有多少朋友、多常被邀請、有沒有被稱讚。

lines.en: I almost the analogy I was thinking of then is it's almost like you either think you're a bird or you think you're on a roller coaster.
lines.zh: 我剛剛想到的比喻是，你要嘛覺得自己是一隻鳥，要嘛覺得自己在坐雲霄飛車。

lines.en: Tell me more. You know, a roller coaster has a fixed track
lines.zh: 多說一點。你知道，雲霄飛車有固定的軌道，

lines.en: really irrespective of what you do.
lines.zh: 不管你做什麼都一樣。

lines.en: It's going to go up, down, left, right, spin, and you're just holding on and going with it.
lines.zh: 它會上、下、左、右、旋轉，而你只能抓緊、跟著它走。

lines.en: Whereas a bird feels like it has the agency to go go anywhere. No rail. Yeah. M.
lines.zh: 而鳥會覺得自己有能力想去哪就去哪。沒有軌道。對。嗯。

lines.en: And some people I think do think that they're on a roller coaster. Yeah. On a track.
lines.zh: 而我覺得有些人確實覺得自己在坐雲霄飛車。對。在軌道上。

lines.en: I mean, look, I don't want to get too deep, but if we were in a normal conversation, I would ask you about fate.
lines.zh: 我是說，聽著，我不想講得太深，但如果我們是在正常的對話中，我會問你關於命運的事。

lines.en: You know, I think there's questions that can we begin to uncover someone's level three.
lines.zh: 你知道，我覺得有一些問題可以讓我們開始發掘一個人的第三層。

lines.en: Do you believe in luck?
lines.zh: 你相信運氣嗎？

lines.en: Do you believe you're lucky?
lines.zh: 你相信自己很幸運嗎？

lines.en: Do you believe in fate?
lines.zh: 你相信命運嗎？

lines.en: I think if you believe in fate, you're more likely to believe that you're on a roller coaster. that you're on a ride that is predetermined and now it's up and then it's going to go down and they're going to have a loop.
lines.zh: 我覺得如果你相信命運，你比較可能相信自己在坐雲霄飛車，相信自己在一段注定好的旅程上，現在往上，接著會往下，然後會有一個大迴圈。

lines.en: So, I wonder I don't know if someone has a high belief in faith or predetermined fate if they would feel an external locus of control and maybe that wouldn't be as good for their mental health.
lines.zh: 所以我在想，我不知道，如果有人非常相信命運或宿命，他們會不會有外在控制感，而那也許對他們的心理健康不太好。

lines.en: I wonder
lines.zh: 我在想。

lines.en: So, going back to this idea of these contaminators.
lines.zh: 所以回到這些污染型的人。

lines.en: So, we're listening for narrative hints and we can ask questions like are you lucky?
lines.zh: 我們在聽敘事線索，我們可以問這樣的問題：你是幸運的人嗎？

lines.en: By the way, if you ask this question, it's it's a it's a sneaker because it sounds so casual when you ask are you lucky, but their answer really matters.
lines.zh: 順帶一提，如果你問這個問題，它是一匹黑馬，因為當你問「你幸運嗎」時聽起來很隨意，但他們的答案真的很重要。

lines.en: Either there's three answers for are you lucky. One, oh yes. Yes, I feel lucky.
lines.zh: 「你幸運嗎」有三種答案。第一種：喔，是的。是的，我覺得很幸運。

lines.en: When I asked you this last time, you said yes. Yeah.
lines.zh: 我上次問你的時候，你說是。對。

lines.en: I think I I can't look at I feel like I have so much privilege in my life that I feel like I have I am lucky.
lines.zh: 我覺得我沒辦法……我覺得我人生中有這麼多優勢，所以我覺得我很幸運。

lines.en: Yes. Yes. I feel the same.
lines.zh: 對。對。我也有同感。

lines.en: I'm just I'm so grateful, right, that I get to have this super unique career. So I feel lucky. You feel lucky.
lines.zh: 我真的很感恩，對吧，能擁有這麼獨特的事業。所以我覺得很幸運。你覺得很幸運。

lines.en: So yes, if someone says yes right away, that tells you a lot about them.
lines.zh: 所以如果有人馬上說是，這會告訴你很多關於他們的事。

lines.en: That means they probably have a high amount of gratitude.
lines.zh: 這代表他們大概有很高的感恩心。

lines.en: They probably have a high amount of control or agency. and they also have confidence
lines.zh: 他們大概有很高的掌控感或主導權，而且他們也有自信，

lines.en: because it's the the quickness the speed of their answer matters here then there are people who are going to go what no I I don't think I'm lucky now this is a really important thing to know about them
lines.zh: 因為回答得多快、速度在這裡很重要。然後有些人會說：什麼？不，我不覺得我很幸運。這是關於他們非常重要的資訊，

lines.en: and I I don't think you should try to change it right
lines.zh: 而我不覺得你應該試著去改變它，對吧？

lines.en: like I think that that's a version of toxic positivity telling someone oh but you're so lucky you know think of all the things that you should be grateful for usually
lines.zh: 我覺得那是一種有毒的正能量，跟對方說：喔，可是你很幸運啊，想想所有你應該感恩的事。通常

lines.en: that actually makes someone dig in it makes them feel very misunderstood you're the best thing you can do if someone says they don't feel lucky is to understand it.
lines.zh: 那反而會讓對方更固執，讓他們覺得非常被誤解。如果有人說他們不覺得幸運，你能做的最好的事就是去理解。

lines.en: Why? What are the forces? When did that happen?
lines.zh: 為什麼？是什麼力量造成的？什麼時候發生的？

lines.en: Did you ever feel lucky before?
lines.zh: 你以前覺得幸運過嗎？

lines.en: Sometimes people can flip from lucky to unlucky with a very bad circumstance.
lines.zh: 有時候人會因為一個非常糟的遭遇，從幸運翻轉成不幸。

lines.en: And it is crucial that you understand that before you judge it. So curiosity gets engaged.
lines.zh: 在你評判之前先理解這一點，至關重要。所以要啟動好奇心。

lines.en: If someone says they're unlucky, I think that's an opportunity to really reach out and meet someone where they're at because in that moment they might.
lines.zh: 如果有人說他們很不幸，我覺得那是一個機會，真正去接觸他們、在他們所在的地方與他們相遇，因為在那一刻他們可能……

lines.en: Are you going to disagree with me? No, no, no.
lines.zh: 你要反駁我嗎？不不不。

lines.en: I was just thinking about how wonderful of a question that is for when you first meet someone in in an interview or a first date.
lines.zh: 我只是在想，在面試或第一次約會剛認識一個人時，這是一個多棒的問題。

lines.en: I was like maybe I should ask people in an interview.
lines.zh: 我在想也許我應該在面試時問大家。

lines.en: Do you think you're lucky? You should
lines.zh: 你覺得你幸運嗎？你應該問。

lines.en: cuz what what is that revealing if they say yes? It's revealing multitudes, right?
lines.zh: 因為如果他們說是，那透露了什麼？透露了很多東西，對吧？

lines.en: Their gratitude, their perspective on life, their internal locus of control. You're an optimist often.
lines.zh: 他們的感恩心、他們的人生觀、他們的內在控制感。你常常是樂觀的人。

lines.en: Not always, but often sometimes it can be realists. Okay? Right?
lines.zh: 不一定，但通常是，有時也可能是現實主義者。好嗎？對吧？

lines.en: Like I am objectively lucky because I have all these things that can be realist.
lines.zh: 就像我客觀來說很幸運，因為我擁有這些東西，那可以是現實主義者。

lines.en: But man, you're going to learn a lot.
lines.zh: 但天啊，你會了解很多。

lines.en: You're the whole point of level three is predicting behavior.
lines.zh: 第三層的整個重點就是預測行為。

lines.en: If you know their luck, you're going to be able to predict a lot of how they are in a relationship, how they are as a friend, how they are going to be at work,
lines.zh: 如果你知道他們的運氣觀，你就能預測他們在感情中是什麼樣子、作為朋友是什麼樣子、在職場上會是什麼樣子，

lines.en: right? Fate, I think, is an interesting one to ask someone.
lines.zh: 對吧？我覺得命運是一個很有意思的問題。

lines.en: And then there's other questions that seem silly but actually have tremendous meaning.
lines.zh: 還有其他看似很蠢、其實意義重大的問題。

lines.en: And level three is all about meaning.
lines.zh: 而第三層就是關於意義。

lines.en: Okay, so the third answer for lucky thank you is that person who is afraid to answer.
lines.zh: 好，關於幸運的第三種答案，謝謝，是那種不敢回答的人。

lines.en: And I have asked this question of thousands of people and you get this bucket of um well kind of.
lines.zh: 我問過幾千個人這個問題，會有一群人說：嗯，算是吧。

lines.en: Now this is very interesting because this tells you they're probably not that introspective.
lines.zh: 這非常有意思，因為這告訴你他們大概不太會自我反省。

lines.en: So one of two things they actually don't know.
lines.zh: 所以有兩種可能，一是他們其實不知道。

lines.en: They they literally have not ever thought about it and they will say to you I've never thought about and they're literally sitting in front of you reanalyzing their entire life trying to answer this question for you.
lines.zh: 他們真的從來沒想過，他們會跟你說：我從來沒想過，然後他們就坐在你面前重新分析自己的整個人生，想回答你這個問題。

lines.en: They've never considered it. So that's also helpful. That's helpful.
lines.zh: 他們從來沒思考過。所以這也很有幫助。很有幫助。

lines.en: You know, if you're in a relationship and someone's not that introspective, that's good to know.
lines.zh: 你知道，如果你在一段感情中，而對方不太會自我反省，知道這點很好。

lines.en: Not good or bad, just good to know, especially if you value that.
lines.zh: 沒有好壞，只是知道很好，尤其如果你重視這一點。

lines.en: Like introspection is one of my core values.
lines.zh: 像自我反省是我的核心價值之一。

lines.en: So, you know, that might might not be bode well for me.
lines.zh: 所以，你知道，那可能對我來說不是好兆頭。

lines.en: Or second, they don't feel safe with you yet.
lines.zh: 第二種可能是，他們跟你在一起還不覺得安全。

lines.en: It can be a hint that you went too too fast.
lines.zh: 這可能是一個線索，表示你太快了。

lines.en: If someone says I kind of or I'm not sure, you might have jumped to level three too quickly and they are not ready to share or they are embarrassed about something.
lines.zh: 如果有人說「算是吧」或「我不確定」，你可能太快跳到第三層，他們還沒準備好分享，或是他們對某件事感到難為情。

lines.en: They have shame or they have something in their past that they feel is very unlucky but they don't feel ready to share it.
lines.zh: 他們有羞愧感，或過去有某件他們覺得非常不幸的事，但還沒準備好分享。

lines.en: Have they done studies on this this particular question?
lines.zh: 有人針對這個特定問題做過研究嗎？

lines.en: I think only we have. Only you have.
lines.zh: 我想只有我們做過。只有你們做過。

lines.en: Richard Wiseman has done a lot of research on luck specifically and he he there's like a luck test you can give someone.
lines.zh: Richard Wiseman 針對運氣做過很多研究，他有一個可以給人做的運氣測驗。

lines.en: We did this in our in our lab.
lines.zh: 我們在我們的實驗室做過。

lines.en: So, it's a official luck test to see how lucky you think you are.
lines.zh: 所以那是一個正式的運氣測驗，看你覺得自己有多幸運。

lines.en: It's like a 10 question diagnostic and it asks all these different variations of that question.
lines.zh: 大概是 10 題的診斷測驗，會問這個問題的各種不同變化。

lines.en: So, it is academically studied.
lines.zh: 所以它是有學術研究的。

lines.en: But I don't think what's studied, at least not yet, is how your answer is going to dictate your life.
lines.zh: 但我覺得還沒有被研究、至少目前還沒有的，是你的答案會如何主導你的人生。

lines.en: Like I would love to know maybe future research in our lab is if you consider yourself very lucky, do you make more money?
lines.zh: 我很想知道，也許是我們實驗室未來的研究：如果你覺得自己非常幸運，你會賺比較多錢嗎？

lines.en: Do you make less money? Is there any income? Are you older? Are you younger?
lines.zh: 你會賺比較少錢嗎？跟收入有關嗎？你年紀比較大嗎？比較年輕嗎？

lines.en: Are you a child of privilege or not?
lines.zh: 你是不是出身優渥？

lines.en: So, I I think it's coming.
lines.zh: 所以我覺得這會來的。

lines.en: I mean, I think that's where this excitement kind of comes from.
lines.zh: 我是說，我覺得這就是這份興奮感的來源。

lines.en: At least it gets me excited as a as a behavior researcher.
lines.zh: 至少身為行為研究者，這讓我很興奮。

lines.en: I I was just looking at that study by Dr. Richard Wiseman.
lines.zh: 我剛剛在看 Richard Wiseman 博士的那項研究。

lines.en: He discovered that people who answer yes, I am lucky actually generate their own good fortune by acting very acting in very specific ways.
lines.zh: 他發現回答「是，我很幸運」的人，其實是透過非常特定的行為方式，替自己創造好運。

lines.en: They have lower anxiety. They have higher extraversion.
lines.zh: 他們焦慮程度比較低，外向程度比較高。

lines.en: They tend to talk talk to lots of people and make lots of friendships and relationships.
lines.zh: 他們往往會跟很多人聊天，建立很多友誼和關係。

lines.en: High openness to experience, relentless optimism. That's very very interesting.
lines.zh: 對經驗的開放程度很高，有不屈不撓的樂觀。這非常非常有意思。

lines.en: I I have considered I've really considered this doing a luck workshop where all I do in the workshop is help you harvest your own feelings of luck.
lines.zh: 我考慮過，我真的考慮過辦一個運氣工作坊，在工作坊裡我只做一件事，就是幫你收集你自己的幸運感。

lines.en: It is so healing. It is so fulfilling to feel lucky to wake up in the day and feel lucky.
lines.zh: 這非常療癒。一早醒來覺得自己很幸運，真的非常充實。

lines.en: It's better than gratitude, right?
lines.zh: 這比感恩還好，對吧？

lines.en: Gratitude is sort of shaming in its own way.
lines.zh: 感恩某種程度上有點讓人羞愧的意味。

lines.en: I'm like kind of anti-gratitude, but feeling like you're really really lucky is is so empowering.
lines.zh: 我有點反對感恩，但覺得自己真的真的很幸運，是非常有力量的。

lines.en: And so I've thought about creating luck labs,
lines.zh: 所以我想過創立「幸運實驗室」，

lines.en: like a little luck workshop where you can come and we're going to we're going to convince you that you're lucky because it's that good of an investment in your in your feelings of happiness.
lines.zh: 像一個小小的幸運工作坊，你可以來，我們會說服你你很幸運，因為這對你的幸福感是非常好的投資。

lines.en: I I would like to ask the audience, I'm just super interested.
lines.zh: 我想問問觀眾，我真的超有興趣。

lines.en: I would like to ask all the uh people listening now if they do you guys feel lucky and I would like honest answers in the comment section.
lines.zh: 我想問所有正在聽的人：你們覺得自己幸運嗎？我想在留言區看到誠實的回答。

lines.en: And don't I know you just heard us say that lucky people are going to have uh have better lives.
lines.zh: 我知道你們剛聽我們說幸運的人會有比較好的人生。

lines.en: Just be completely honest just for pure research purposes.
lines.zh: 就完全誠實，純粹為了研究目的。

lines.en: And do you know what?
lines.zh: 你知道嗎？

lines.en: I know people that don't feel lucky are going to be honest because
lines.zh: 我知道不覺得幸運的人會很誠實，因為

lines.en: they're going to be honest and they're going to tell you exactly why.
lines.zh: 他們會很誠實，而且會告訴你確切的原因。

lines.en: And they're going to get really mad at us because they're going to say that something really bad happened to them and how dare we tell them that luck is good.
lines.zh: 他們會很氣我們，因為他們會說他們發生過很糟的事，我們怎麼敢說運氣是好的。

lines.en: That's what's going to happen cuz I've I've heard them do it.
lines.zh: 一定會這樣，因為我聽過他們這樣說。

lines.en: Can you get mad at Vanessa and not me? I'm
lines.zh: 你們可以氣 Vanessa 就好，不要氣我嗎？我……

lines.en: No, get mad at him. No, it's fine.
lines.zh: 不，氣他。不，沒關係。

lines.en: You can get mad at me. It's fine. I have no shell.
lines.zh: 你們可以氣我。沒關係。我沒有防護殼。

lines.en: But but but this is why I'm asking because I want to I want to I'm coming from one perspective from one experience that I've had in my life and I feel like I am grateful and I've been very privileged.
lines.zh: 但這就是我問的原因，因為我想……我是從一個角度、從我人生中的一種經驗出發，我覺得我很感恩，也一直很有優勢。

lines.en: So I would like to understand why other people do not feel lucky in their lives and you know I I guess it would also be surprising to hear
lines.zh: 所以我想了解為什麼其他人不覺得自己的人生幸運，而且，你知道，我猜也會很驚訝地聽到

lines.en: that some people have been through objectively horrific things but they some of them might still feel lucky.
lines.zh: 有些人經歷過客觀來說很可怕的事，但其中有些人可能仍然覺得幸運。

lines.en: So that would be interesting as well.
lines.zh: 所以那也會很有意思。

lines.en: So I'll be reading the comments
lines.zh: 所以我會看留言。

lines.en: and that is also fact versus frame. Okay. Right.
lines.zh: 這也是「事實 vs. 框架」。好。對。

lines.en: So the way that we begin to rewrite our story and I believe so much in self- authorship, right?
lines.zh: 所以我們開始改寫自己故事的方式，而我非常相信「自我書寫」，對吧？

lines.en: Yes, there's a story you tell yourself about yourself, but you also are the author of your own life, right?
lines.zh: 對，有一個你告訴自己關於自己的故事，但你也是自己人生的作者，對吧？

lines.en: You're the author of your own narrative.
lines.zh: 你是自己敘事的作者。

lines.en: The way that we begin to take up the pen, like become the author of our own life, is we ask ourselves questions about why do I have that idea?
lines.zh: 我們開始拿起筆、成為自己人生作者的方式，就是問自己：我為什麼會有這個想法？

lines.en: What is the evidence for that idea?
lines.zh: 這個想法的證據是什麼？

lines.en: The facts might be there, but our frame of them is different.
lines.zh: 事實可能存在，但我們看待它的框架不同。

lines.en: So, for example, take a breakup.
lines.zh: 例如，拿分手來說。

lines.en: And I can almost always find out someone's contamination or redemption narrative if I ask them about a breakup.
lines.zh: 如果我問一個人關於分手的事，我幾乎總能看出他是污染敘事還是救贖敘事。

lines.en: People with contamination narratives will almost always say, "The breakup nearly destroyed me."
lines.zh: 有污染敘事的人幾乎總會說：「那次分手差點毀了我。」

lines.en: The I don't trust men anymore.
lines.zh: 「我再也不相信男人了。

lines.en: I don't trust women anymore.
lines.zh: 我再也不相信女人了。

lines.en: You know, it just it it just took from me.
lines.zh: 你知道，它就是把我的東西都奪走了。

lines.en: I feel like a shell of myself.
lines.zh: 我覺得自己只剩一副空殼。」

lines.en: And it stays that way.
lines.zh: 而且一直都是那樣。

lines.en: Everyone has a period of a bad breakup time, but they never get through that.
lines.zh: 每個人都會有一段分手後很難熬的時期，但他們永遠走不出來。

lines.en: That they feel like that that breakup fundamentally changed them for the worse.
lines.zh: 他們覺得那次分手從根本上把他們變得更糟。

lines.en: Whereas someone with a a positive or a redemption narrative, even if it was a horrific breakup, they'll say, "I will never do that again."
lines.zh: 而有正向或救贖敘事的人，就算那是一次很可怕的分手，他們會說：「我再也不會那樣做了。」

lines.en: That made me stronger. It was horrible.
lines.zh: 「那讓我更堅強。那很可怕。

lines.en: It was one of the worst times of my life, but I know now who not to choose, and I know who to choose.
lines.zh: 那是我人生中最糟的時期之一，但我現在知道不該選誰、該選誰。

lines.en: It made me feel stronger. It's that anti-fragile piece.
lines.zh: 它讓我覺得更堅強。」這就是那種反脆弱的部分。

lines.en: Would you give someone a second date if on the first date they turned to you and when you asked them the question, "Are you a lucky person?"
lines.zh: 如果第一次約會時，你問對方「你是幸運的人嗎？」

lines.en: They went, "Absolutely not." I probably wouldn't.
lines.zh: 他們說「完全不是」，你會跟他們第二次約會嗎？我大概不會。

lines.en: You are going to be so mad. You are so cooked.
lines.zh: 你會被罵翻。你完蛋了。

lines.en: They are going to get you. Get it, guys. You were so single. You were so cooked. It's a hypothetical. It was a trap.
lines.zh: 他們會找你算帳。上啊，各位。你會一直單身。你完蛋了。這只是假設。那是個陷阱。

lines.en: That's what it was. You're so mean.
lines.zh: 就是這樣。你好壞。

lines.en: You're like, "Look, throwing us into the fire." Well, don't worry.
lines.zh: 你就像：「你看，把我們丟進火坑。」嗯，別擔心。

lines.en: I got a wine bottle coming. So, no.
lines.zh: 我有一瓶酒要送來。所以不會。

lines.en: I I was thinking I was thinking No.
lines.zh: 我在想，我在想，不會。

lines.en: Would you Gosh, I'm going to ask you now.
lines.zh: 你會……天啊，我現在要問你。

lines.en: If someone if I was on a first date and I said, "Are you a lucky person?" and they said to me, "Absolutely not."
lines.zh: 如果我在第一次約會問：「你是幸運的人嗎？」對方跟我說：「完全不是。」

lines.en: Okay, I'd be curious. Sure, of course.
lines.zh: 好，我會很好奇。當然。

lines.en: And I would want to hear what they would leave.
lines.zh: 我會想聽聽他們……

lines.en: I wouldn't leave the date.
lines.zh: 我不會離開那場約會。

lines.en: But if they were then just like extremely pessimistic, I would probably arrive at this assumption that this is probably not going to be a match cuz that's not my inclination.
lines.zh: 但如果他們接著就是極度悲觀，我大概會得出一個假設：這大概不會是適合的對象，因為那不是我的傾向。

lines.en: And it doesn't it takes too much energy out of me.
lines.zh: 那會消耗我太多能量。

lines.en: And that is also because I think this is beautiful bridge to the next concept.
lines.zh: 而這也是因為，我覺得這是通往下一個概念的絕佳橋梁。

lines.en: Once you begin to uncover these narrative hints, okay, you're talking about luck, you're talking about redemption or contamination narrative.
lines.zh: 一旦你開始發掘這些敘事線索，好，你在談運氣，你在談救贖或污染敘事。

lines.en: I believe and this is more art than science that there are five archetypes of these stories.
lines.zh: 我相信，這比較是藝術而非科學，這些故事有五種原型。

lines.en: So I have harvested hundreds, I wouldn't say thousands, hundreds of narratives.
lines.zh: 所以我收集了幾百個，不到幾千，幾百個敘事。

lines.en: It's actually quite hard to ask someone what is your self-narrative?
lines.zh: 要直接問一個人「你的自我敘事是什麼？」其實相當困難。

lines.en: It's very hard question, but there are questions that we can begin to talk about that that do harvest it. I notice patterns.
lines.zh: 那是非常困難的問題，但有一些問題我們可以開始聊，確實能收集到它。我注意到一些模式。

lines.en: There are the same narratives over and over again, and there about five of them.
lines.zh: 同樣的敘事一再出現，大概有五種。

lines.en: I think that we share an archetype. I think we do.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們有同一種原型。我覺得是。

lines.en: Now, maybe I'm flattering myself.
lines.zh: 好，也許我在往自己臉上貼金。

lines.en: So, the first archetype is the ambitious hero.
lines.zh: 第一種原型是「雄心勃勃的英雄」。

lines.en: And I think this is us, but you'll tell me.
lines.zh: 我覺得這就是我們，但你再告訴我。

lines.en: So, the ambitious hero um has had challenges and obstacles, but they feel that their grit and resilience have they've been able to overcome.
lines.zh: 雄心勃勃的英雄，嗯，經歷過挑戰和障礙，但他們覺得自己的毅力和韌性讓他們能克服一切。

lines.en: They struggle because they are never satisfied.
lines.zh: 他們的掙扎在於他們永遠不滿足。

lines.en: And what is an archetype? Like what is I got excited. Yes.
lines.zh: 那什麼是原型？就是……我太興奮了。對。

lines.en: So this is not like a personality type.
lines.zh: 所以這不像是一種人格類型。

lines.en: It's not like Myers-Briggs or Enneagram.
lines.zh: 它不像 MBTI 或九型人格。

lines.en: Those are quite like stable.
lines.zh: 那些相當穩定。

lines.en: This is a fluid archetype of how you're seeing your story in this moment.
lines.zh: 這是一種流動的原型，代表你在此刻如何看待自己的故事。

lines.en: For example, I might ask you if if you had to write a memoir, what would the title of your memoir be?
lines.zh: 例如，我可能會問你：如果你要寫一本回憶錄，書名會是什麼？

lines.en: And this is going to impact how I have conversations with people.
lines.zh: 這會影響我和別人的對話方式。

lines.en: This is going to impact how you have conversations with people. how you behave interpersonally, so how you act at work.
lines.zh: 這會影響你和別人的對話方式、你的人際行為，也就是你在職場上的表現。

lines.en: Like an ambitious hero is going to act very, very differently at work than a contented pragmatist.
lines.zh: 像雄心勃勃的英雄在職場上的表現，會和知足的務實派非常非常不同。

lines.en: And is it going to impact who I'm attracted to platonically and romantically? Absolutely.
lines.zh: 它會影響我在友情和愛情上被誰吸引嗎？絕對會。

lines.en: It dictates your relationship patterns. Okay. Right.
lines.zh: 它主導你的關係模式。好。對。

lines.en: Your conversational patterns, how you converse, how you bond, how you connect, and more importantly, since I'm so interested in work conversations, how you work, how you view effectiveness, how you view efficiency.
lines.zh: 你的對話模式、你怎麼聊天、怎麼建立情感、怎麼連結，更重要的是，因為我對職場對話很有興趣，還有你怎麼工作、怎麼看待成效、怎麼看待效率。

lines.en: My founders, right, ambitious hero founders are going to have the same struggles over and over again.
lines.zh: 我的創辦人們，對吧，雄心勃勃的英雄型創辦人會一再遇到同樣的掙扎。

lines.en: They're going to be very different than the contented pragmatist founder.
lines.zh: 他們會和知足務實派的創辦人非常不同。

lines.en: So the ambitious hero, what's their sort of internal monologue?
lines.zh: 那雄心勃勃的英雄，他們的內在獨白大概是什麼？

lines.en: Their internal monologue is I got this. I can do this. Hustle, hustle more,
lines.zh: 他們的內在獨白是：我搞得定。我做得到。拚，再拚一點，

lines.en: more, bigger, more, bigger, bigger, more.
lines.zh: 更多、更大、更多、更大、更大、更多。

lines.en: I can do that better.
lines.zh: 那個我可以做得更好。

lines.en: I can do that bigger. Right.
lines.zh: 那個我可以做得更大。對。

lines.en: It's like we I get, you know, shiny object syndrome is like one of the nicer ways to talk about ambitious heroes.
lines.zh: 就像是，你知道，「閃亮物品症候群」是形容雄心勃勃的英雄比較好聽的說法之一。

lines.en: You know, shiny object syndrome. No.
lines.zh: 你知道閃亮物品症候群嗎？不知道。

lines.en: It's like a founder who won't stop trying new initiatives and keeps throwing new ideas on the table when they haven't finished their first one. Yeah. Yeah.
lines.zh: 就像一個創辦人一直不停嘗試新計畫，第一個還沒做完就一直丟新點子上桌。對。對。

lines.en: Okay. Do you have that?
lines.zh: 好。你有這個問題嗎？

lines.en: Well, yes, but I have put uh systems in place. Ah, yeah.
lines.zh: 嗯，有，但我設了一些機制。啊，對。

lines.en: To make sure that it doesn't uh sink the company as Jeff Bezos said.
lines.zh: 確保它不會像 Jeff Bezos 說的那樣拖垮公司。

lines.en: Jeff Bezos said, "I've got enough ideas to sink the company and he has to learn to release them at a cadence that the company can tolerate."
lines.zh: Jeff Bezos 說：「我的點子多到足以拖垮公司」，他得學會以公司能承受的節奏釋放那些點子。

lines.zh: 就是，你知道，有點

lines.en: A really critical part of this exercise is that you asked someone about the character and then you say why. What traits?
lines.zh: 這個練習一個非常關鍵的部分，是你問了對方角色之後，要問為什麼。什麼特質？

lines.en: Because the traits that they say next are going to tell you every single thing about that person.
lines.zh: 因為他們接下來說的特質，會告訴你關於那個人的一切。

lines.en: For example, I if I ask someone, you know, what what person are you most like?
lines.zh: 例如，如果我問某人：你最像哪個人？

lines.en: And they say, "Mother Teresa."

lines.en: You know, I might not agree with them.

lines.en: Like, maybe I don't see that, but whatever they say next is going to tell me a lot about how they view themselves, whether it's true or not.
lines.zh: 我可能看不出來，但他們接下來說的，不管是真是假，都會告訴我很多關於他們如何看待自己的事。

lines.en: And this is the hardest part about level three, and it's the most inconvenient part of level three. You probably won't agree. Okay?

lines.en: What character are you most like and why?
lines.zh: 你最像哪個角色？為什麼？

lines.en: Okay, so I relate most with Claire Dunphy from Modern Family, especially in her entrepreneurial years.
lines.zh: 好，我最有共鳴的是《摩登家庭》裡的 Claire Dunphy，尤其是她創業的那幾年。

lines.en: Most people would be surprised that actually identify first as a mother, not an entrepreneur.
lines.zh: 大部分人會很驚訝，其實我首先認同自己是個母親，而不是創業家。

lines.en: Most of my day is with my kids.
lines.zh: 我一天大部分時間都和孩子在一起。

lines.en: Uh I'm a little awkward. I'm very neurotic.
lines.zh: 呃，我有點尷尬，非常神經質。

lines.en: Um and so I resonate most with her.
lines.zh: 嗯，所以我對她最有共鳴。

lines.en: And that um ambitious working mom is sort of what I'm constantly struggling with. Constantly.
lines.zh: 而那種雄心勃勃的職業媽媽，就是我一直在掙扎的。一直在掙扎。

lines.en: Yeah, especially as an ambitious hero because I want to do both perfectly and I I cannot. Yeah.

lines.en: So this is the one way that it can help you some sometimes brainstorm. Okay. The ambitious hero, right? We started with that. Yeah. Archetype number one.
lines.zh: 所以這是它有時能幫你腦力激盪的一個方法。好。雄心勃勃的英雄，對吧？我們從這個開始。對。第一種原型。

lines.zh: 我把它叫做「知足的務實派」。

lines.en: Again, these are a little more art than science.
lines.zh: 再說一次，這些比較像藝術而非科學。

lines.en: The contented pragmatist is somebody who likes it as it is.
lines.zh: 知足的務實派是喜歡維持現狀的人。

lines.en: They are quite content, very happy with where things are.
lines.zh: 他們相當知足，對事情現在的狀態非常滿意。

lines.en: They don't really need to change it if it's not broken.
lines.zh: 如果沒壞，他們就不太需要去改變。

lines.en: They are not very ambitious cuz they're very grounded in where they are.
lines.zh: 他們不太有野心，因為他們對自己所在的位置非常踏實。

lines.en: They love habit and ritual and tradition in conversation relationally.
lines.zh: 在對話和關係中，他們熱愛習慣、儀式和傳統。

lines.en: They struggle when people push them to try harder or do more because they're like, "I'm good. Life is good.

lines.en: and I'm like you should bottle it up and sell it at farmers markets and they're like but why and I'm like but why not right so relationally um they're often seen as unambitious but actually they're just quite content.
